name: Commonwealth of England
alt: Commonwealth of England, Scotland and Ireland

predecessors.name: Kingdom of England
predecessors.text: England, which 'An Act declaring England to be a Commonwealth' (19 May 1649) turned into a republic; Cliopatria's Commonwealth shape of 1645-1648 is Parliament's England and Wales

successors.name: Kingdom of England
successors.text: the restored Stuart monarchy: 'On 8 May 1660, the Convention Parliament declared Charles II the lawful successor of Charles I and king'; Charles II returned on 23 May 1660 and entered London on 29 May

ledger.x: 1649: the Rump Parliament declares England a Commonwealth (19 May).
1649: Cromwell lands at Dublin to reconquer Ireland (15 August).
1650: Kilkenny, the Confederate capital, is captured in March.
1652: Galway falls in May and organised Confederate resistance ends.
May 1652: the last Confederate land passes to the Commonwealth.
1653: Cromwell becomes Lord Protector (16 December): the Protectorate, officially the Commonwealth of England, Scotland and Ireland, lasts until 25 May 1659.
June 1658: Dunkirk is handed to the Protectorate.
1659: Richard Cromwell resigns (25 May) and the Rump Parliament is recalled: the Commonwealth is restored until 1660.
1660: Scotland leaves the Commonwealth with the Restoration; the Kingdom of Scotland page ends the 'incorporation of Scotland into the Commonwealth of England, Scotland and Ireland (1653-1660)'.
1660: the Stuart Restoration ends the Commonwealth.

wars.name: Cromwellian conquest of Ireland
wars.outcome: Commonwealth victory: Kilkenny (March 1650), Waterford (1650), Limerick (1651) and Galway (May 1652) fall; the last organised force surrenders at Cloughoughter on 27 April 1653 and Parliament declares the rebellion subdued on 27 September 1653; Ireland is…

wars.name: Anglo-Scottish War (Third English Civil War)
wars.outcome: Commonwealth victory: Dunbar (3 September 1650), Inverkeithing (20 July 1651), Worcester (3 September 1651) and the fall of Dunnottar (24 May 1652) end Scottish independence; Scotland is incorporated in the Commonwealth.

wars.name: Battle of the Dunes and the Dunkirk award
wars.outcome: Franco-English victory: 'the town of Dunkirk was awarded by France to the Protectorate'; sold back to France by Charles II in 1662.

certainty.note: The Irish and Scottish fronts move year by year (Kilkenny 1650, Limerick 1651, Dunnottar and Galway 1652); only the English coast and the border of 1237 (Treaty of York, Kingdom of Scotland page) are fixed.
One state over the whole of the British Isles, with island coasts as its borders; Dunkirk (1658) is an enclave of uncertain extent.
